newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London little change, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London little change, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. shares struggled for a clear direction on Thursday as investors continued to keep a close watch on bond yields and U.S. treasuries.

With the yield on the benchmark 30-year long bond stubbornly standing above the seven percent level, many European investors were reluctant to take new positions ahead of Wall Street's opening, dealers said.
"The market is basically directionless today. There is little business about," one market maker said.
"The long bond is holding pretty steady but people are still afraid that the yield will creep higher."
U.S. treasuries were slightly firmer with the June T-bond up 5/32 to 108-28/32 while the yield on the long bond stood at 7.03 percent by 1010 GMT.
Only a handful of shares had traded my late morning, dealers said.

Philip Morris Cos Inc eased $1/2 to $43-1/2 after a report in the Wall Street Journal said opposition was building among some state attorneys general against a settlement plan with the tobacco industry that would limit future liability.
RJR Nabisco Holdings was down $1/4 to $32-1/4.
The June S&P 500 futures contract was down 0.65 to 849.90.
